rules.source: RFC 0014 §3 R1, R2, R6, T (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-24 on the cross-version fixture); the red-team inventory, row 1
rules.statement: The CoSec-Identity header is ignorable with must-understand (IDN-41): a reader ignores a member it does not know unless the header's crit names it, which it refuses with 503; a malformed crit is 400; a missing member stays missing, memberships above all (IDN-42); its version v changes only with the major version. What one version of a gateway writes, the other version's receiver reads as the current receiver does. A header that states no auth.kind, as every header of a release before kinds, is a workload's to the current receiver (IDN-44); the current writer's headers, which state it, reach a previous receiver from the first release that ignores a member it does not know (8.0.0-beta.9).
guards: compat:IdentityHeaderCompatTest#each version reads what the other writes as the current reader does
compat:IdentityHeaderCompatTest#a header written without memberships is read without them, never as empty ones
compat:IdentityHeaderCompatTest#a member a later version adds is ignored by every reader, which reads the header it knows
compat:IdentityHeaderCompatTest#a later member crit names is refused as an outage by a reader that does not know it
compat:IdentityHeaderCompatTest#the current reader reads the kind the current writer states, and a header without one as a workload's

rules.source: RFC 0014 §3 R1, R2, R6, T (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-24 on the cross-version fixture); the red-team inventory, row 2
rules.statement: CoSec's access token is ignorable: a verifier reads its named claims and ignores the others, except the claims whose presence refuses the token (cosec.token, act); a missing claim reads as its documented absence, never wider. A token one version issues, the other version verifies as the current verifier does.
guards: compat:TokenCompatTest#each version verifies what the other issues as the current verifier does

rules.source: RFC 0014 §3 R1, R2, R6, T (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-24 on the cross-version fixture); the red-team inventory, row 3
rules.statement: A refresh token is strict: only a token whose cosec.token is refresh is one, and no version takes it for an access token.
guards: compat:TokenCompatTest#a refresh token is refused as an access token by every version

rules.source: RFC 0014 §3 R1, R2, R6, T (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-24 on the cross-version fixture); the red-team inventory, row 4
rules.statement: A session record is ignorable with must-understand (SNP-27, SNP-28) and its format is frozen at 2 within 8.x (SNP-29): each version reads the session the other wrote; a rewrite by either keeps every member the rewriting version knows and drops a later member, leaving the same session; a record whose crit names a member a version does not know is refused by it and never rewritten.
guards: compat:SessionRecordCompatTest#each version reads the session the other wrote
compat:SessionRecordCompatTest#a rewrite by either version keeps every member, and the other reads it
compat:SessionRecordCompatTest#a later member without crit is dropped by a rewrite, which leaves the same session
compat:SessionRecordCompatTest#a record whose crit names a member a version does not know is refused by it, and never rewritten

rules.source: RFC 0014 §3 R1, R2, R6, T (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-24 on the cross-version fixture); the red-team inventory, row 5
rules.statement: The session index is frozen within the major version (RFC 0014 R6, SNP-26): sessions begun half by each version are held to the principal's one limit.
guards: compat:CounterCompatTest#sessions begun half by each version are held to the principal's limit

rules.source: RFC 0014 §3 R1, R2, R6, T (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-24 on the cross-version fixture); the red-team inventory, row 6
rules.statement: Revocations are frozen within the major version (RFC 0014 R6, SNP-26): a revocation not read is a token accepted again, so what either version writes, the other reads.
guards: compat:CredentialCompatTest#a revocation either version writes, the other reads

rules.source: RFC 0014 §3 R1, R2, R6, T (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-24 on the cross-version fixture); the red-team inventory, row 7
rules.statement: An API key record is strict (format 3, exactly its fields): what either version saves, the other reads alike.
guards: compat:CredentialCompatTest#an API key either version saves, the other reads alike

rules.source: RFC 0014 §3 R1, R2, R6, T (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-24 on the cross-version fixture); the red-team inventory, row 8
rules.statement: Rate limit counters are frozen within the major version (RFC 0014 R6, SNP-26): requests split between two versions on one rule get no more than one version alone allows.
guards: compat:CounterCompatTest#a rate limit taken half by each version allows no more than its quota

rules.source: RFC 0014 §3 R1, R2, R6, T (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-24 on the cross-version fixture); the red-team inventory, row 9
rules.statement: Social login states and their count are frozen within the major version (RFC 0014 R6, SNP-26): states recorded by either version are counted together, and one version takes what the other recorded.
guards: compat:CounterCompatTest#login states are counted together, and one version takes what the other recorded

rules.source: RFC 0014 §3 R1, R2, R6, T (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-24 on the cross-version fixture); the red-team inventory, row 11
rules.statement: Policy documents are strict (schema 2) and their feature level rises for anything that changes an older reader's decision or makes it refuse (RFC 0014 R4): a document either version compiles, the other compiles too; a pattern a later version reserves (DOC-15), an earlier one took as a literal, and the later one refuses.
guards: compat:DocumentCompatTest#a document either version compiles, the other compiles too
compat:DocumentCompatTest#a pattern the current version reserves is refused by it, though the previous one took it as a literal

rules.source: RFC 0014 §3 R1, R2, R6, T (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-24 on the cross-version fixture); the red-team inventory, row 12
rules.statement: A staged candidate record is ignorable with must-understand (SNP-27, SNP-28); its document stays strict (SNP-12).
guards: compat:RecordCompatTest#each version reads and writes back the record the other wrote, unchanged
compat:RecordCompatTest#a later member without crit is dropped by a rewrite, which leaves the same record
compat:RecordCompatTest#a record whose crit names a member a version does not know is refused by it

rules.source: RFC 0014 §3 R1, R2, R6, T (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-24 on the cross-version fixture); the red-team inventory, row 13
rules.statement: An instance's status, its resident documents and a shadow report are ignorable with must-understand (SNP-27, SNP-28).
guards: compat:RecordCompatTest#each version reads and writes back the record the other wrote, unchanged
compat:RecordCompatTest#a later member without crit is dropped by a rewrite, which leaves the same record
compat:RecordCompatTest#a record whose crit names a member a version does not know is refused by it

rules.source: RFC 0014 §3 R1, R2, R6, T (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-24 on the cross-version fixture); the red-team inventory, row 14
rules.statement: A change record and a staging slot are ignorable with must-understand (SNP-27, SNP-28); a change's operations stay strict (CTL-53).
guards: compat:RecordCompatTest#each version reads and writes back the record the other wrote, unchanged
compat:RecordCompatTest#a later member without crit is dropped by a rewrite, which leaves the same record
compat:RecordCompatTest#a record whose crit names a member a version does not know is refused by it

rules.source: RFC 0014 §3 R1, R2, R6, T (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-24 on the cross-version fixture); the red-team inventory, row 22
rules.statement: What CoCache keeps around a value in Redis is read alike by both versions' CoCache: the cross-version tests read and write every store through each version's own CoCache, the previous release loaded as published, and a case that holds only from a later release must still fail against an earlier baseline.
guards: compat:SideIsolationTest#the previous side runs the published release and the current side this build
compat:SideIsolationTest#neither version is visible to the test's own class loader
compat:BaselineTest#a case before its release must fail, and one that already holds says so
compat:SessionRecordCompatTest#each version reads the session the other wrote

rules.source: RFC 0014 §3 R1, R2, R6, T (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-24 on phase 2 of the cross-version fixture); the red-team inventory, row 10
rules.statement: Memberships are not exchanged between instances: each holds its own, for cosec.authorization.membership.ttl, and none is written to Redis; what crosses is their invalidation, a frame on the deployment's membership channel, which an instance of either version applies to its own copy.
guards: compat:LocalStateCompatTest#an invalidation either version publishes drops the other's copy of a membership

rules.source: RFC 0014 §3 R1, R2, R6, T (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-24 on phase 2 of the cross-version fixture); the red-team inventory, row 15
rules.statement: A document's revision index and the app list are ignorable with must-understand (SNP-27, SNP-28): read alike by both versions' control stores, rewritten unchanged, a later member dropped by a rewrite that leaves the same record, and a record whose crit names a member a version does not know refused by it and never rewritten.
guards: compat:ControlStoreCompatTest#each version reads the record alike, and reads it again after the other rewrote it
compat:ControlStoreCompatTest#a later member without crit is dropped by a rewrite, which leaves the same record
compat:ControlStoreCompatTest#a record whose crit names a member a version does not know is refused by it, and never rewritten

rules.source: RFC 0014 §3 R1, R2, R6, T (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-24 on phase 2 of the cross-version fixture); the red-team inventory, row 16
rules.statement: A control API request is strict: an operation either version's control-sdk writes, either version's control plane reads alike, and one with a member a control plane does not know is refused by it (400), never read as an operation that does less.
guards: compat:ControlApiCompatTest#a proposal either version's client writes, either version's control plane reads alike
compat:ControlApiCompatTest#an operation with a member a control plane does not know is refused by it

rules.source: RFC 0014 §3 R1, R2, R6, T (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-24 on phase 2 of the cross-version fixture); the red-team inventory, row 17
rules.statement: A control API answer is read leniently by control-sdk, a member it does not know ignored, except a document's entries, read strictly so that applying back what was read never drops a member (CTL-76): an answer either version's control plane gives, either version's client reads alike.
guards: compat:ControlApiCompatTest#an answer either version's control plane gives, either version's client reads alike, ignoring a later member
compat:ControlApiCompatTest#a document's entries in an answer are read strictly by every client

rules.source: RFC 0014 §3 R1, R2, R6, T (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-24 on phase 2 of the cross-version fixture); the red-team inventory, row 18
rules.statement: A client meets both versions during a rolling upgrade: every problem the previous version answers it with, with its status, type and title, the current one answers alike; a later version may add a problem, never remove or change one. Within one version contract/ pins every answer (PIP-25).
guards: compat:EdgeCompatTest#every problem the previous version answers a client with, the current one answers alike

rules.source: RFC 0014 §3 R1, R2, R6, T (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-24 on phase 2 of the cross-version fixture); the red-team inventory, row 19
rules.statement: A route map is not exchanged: each instance reads its own file (cosec.authorization.routes.location) at startup, so two versions meet only through the same file rolled out to both, which they resolve alike.
guards: compat:LocalStateCompatTest#one route map is resolved alike by both versions

rules.source: RFC 0014 §3 R1, R2, R6, T (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-24 on phase 2 of the cross-version fixture); the red-team inventory, row 20
rules.statement: Kafka events are not exchanged between versions of CoSec: CoSec writes decision and change events for consumers outside it and reads none back, so their payload is a contract with those consumers only.
guards: compat:LocalStateCompatTest#no module of CoSec consumes Kafka

rules.source: RFC 0014 §3 R1, R2, R6, T (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-24 on phase 2 of the cross-version fixture); the red-team inventory, row 21
rules.statement: The CoSec-* request parameters are strict: both versions read them alike, and one stated twice in disagreement is refused (400) by both.
guards: compat:EdgeCompatTest#the CoSec parameters are read alike, and an ambiguous one refused, by both versions
